Member ID: W601208268
Reference number: POC-0948C5760B-46622
Date of denial notice: 2026-08-06
Procedure at issue: CPT 29881 (knee arthroscopy/meniscus surgery)
Treating surgeon: Okafor, MD, Orthopedic Surgery [NPI/contact number to be inserted]

To the MedStar Family Choice DC Appeals Committee:

I am writing to appeal the denial of prior authorization for CPT 29881 described in the above-referenced Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination. The notice states that the request is denied because "the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure," and that the determination was made "under the plan's applicable medical policy and clinical review criteria." This letter, together with the enclosed clinical records, responds directly to that stated reason and requests reversal of the denial.

**1. No procedure-specific medical policy has been identified or provided.**

I have been unable to locate, and MedStar Family Choice DC's own list of published Medical Policies and Procedures does not include, any medical policy specific to knee arthroscopy, meniscus repair, meniscectomy, or CPT 29881. Because the denial notice does not cite a specific policy number, section, or clinical criterion, I am unable to know precisely which "imaging findings" the reviewer found lacking or what standard was applied. MedStar Family Choice DC's own Utilization Management Criteria policy (Policy #115.DC) states that, absent a service-specific medical policy, "MedStar Family Choice DC prior-authorization decisions for medical and behavioral health services, including residential treatment are based on the following criteria: a. MedStar Family Choice DC Protocols b. MedStar Family Choice DC Pharmacy Policies and Procedures c. InterQual d. American Society of Addiction Medicine (ASAM) e. Medicare and Medicaid Guidelines f. Department of Healthcare Finance (DHCF) Contract, Transmittals and Policies g. MedStar Family Choice DC Managed Care Plan (MCP) benefit coverage h. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) Approval… p. In the absence of guidelines, we use prevailing medical literature from studies and journals."

I have not been furnished the specific InterQual (or other) criteria applied to my case. The same policy states that "All criteria applied in utilization management are available upon request. The request can be made independent of a specific case," and the plan's provider utilization-management page states that "Providers may request the UM criteria utilized for a specific case by calling the MedStar Family Choice DC Clinical Operations Department at 855-798-4244." I am formally requesting, as part of this appeal, a copy of the specific criteria set (including the exact clinical elements it requires) that was applied to deny my request, and an explanation of exactly which imaging finding was considered insufficient. Beyond the language quoted above, I have not been able to obtain the underlying InterQual (or other) clinical criteria text itself, and I am not quoting or characterizing that content because I have not seen it — I am asking the plan to produce it so that I, and my surgeon, can respond to it specifically.

**2. The clinical record supports medical necessity of CPT 29881.**

Regardless of the specific criteria applied, the following facts from my medical record directly address the concern that "imaging findings... do not support medical necessity" and the general prerequisites typically required for meniscal surgery (symptom duration, imaging pathology, functional impairment, and failed conservative care):

- **Symptom duration:** I have had 24 months of progressive knee pain that is unrelieved by rest.
- **Imaging findings:** MRI of the knee performed 2026-05-28 shows a displaced bucket-handle tear of the medial meniscus with mechanical locking. This is a structural, surgically correctable lesion, not an incidental or degenerative finding; the accompanying Kellgren-Lawrence grade 1 (preserved articular cartilage) shows that my knee does not have advanced arthritis that would make meniscal surgery futile — if anything, it supports that surgery is more, not less, likely to help, since the joint surface itself is largely preserved.
- **Failed conservative treatment:** I completed 16 weeks (20 visits) of supervised physical therapy focused on quadriceps strengthening and range of motion, from 2026-03-10 to 2026-06-30, as documented in the physical therapy discharge note. I also used NSAIDs for 6 months with inadequate relief, and received a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-26 that gave only 2 weeks of partial relief. Conservative management has therefore been fully attempted and has failed to resolve my symptoms.
- **Functional impairment:** I continue to experience locking and giving way of the knee, cannot squat or kneel, and am limited to level walking only.
- **Exam findings:** Physical examination documents positive provocative testing on the affected side and range of motion limited by pain, consistent with the MRI findings of a displaced, locking meniscal tear.
- **No contraindications to surgery:** There is no active infection, no untreated substance use, my BMI is 29, and I am a non-smoker.

Taken together, these records show a mechanically significant, imaging-confirmed meniscal tear causing locking and functional disability, in a patient who has completed and failed an adequate trial of conservative care, with no medical contraindication to surgery. I am asking the plan to explain, specifically, why these findings — particularly the documented mechanical locking associated with a displaced bucket-handle tear — were determined not to support medical necessity, and to identify any additional documentation that would change that determination.

**3. Enclosed records.**

I am enclosing the following documentation in support of this appeal:
- MRI report of the knee, dated 2026-05-28
- Physical therapy discharge note documenting the course of care from 2026-03-10 to 2026-06-30
- Documentation of NSAID trial and the corticosteroid injection administered 2026-05-26
- Office/exam notes documenting provocative testing and range-of-motion findings
- [Letter of medical necessity from Dr. Okafor, if separately prepared]
- A copy of this Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination

**4. Requested action and timing.**

I ask that MedStar Family Choice DC reverse the denial and authorize CPT 29881, or, in the alternative, arrange a peer-to-peer conversation between Dr. Okafor and the reviewing Medical Director before a final decision is issued, as your own utilization management policy provides for such discussion prior to a medical necessity denial.

I note that the denial notice states I have 180 days from 2026-08-06 (until 2027-02-02) to appeal, but that MedStar Family Choice DC's published appeals procedure for enrollees states that "[a]ll enrollee appeals must be submitted in writing within 60 calendar days from the date on the Adverse Benefit Determination (denial) notice." Because these two statements conflict, I am submitting this appeal well within 60 calendar days of the notice date, out of caution, and I ask MedStar Family Choice DC to confirm in writing which deadline governs my case.

I understand from your published procedure that required documentation for an enrollee appeal includes the "Medicaid Appeal Form," an "Explanation for the appeal," a "Provider Permission Form for Member Appeals" (if applicable), and "Clinical information (medical records) for date of service." I am [enclosing a completed Medicaid Appeal Form / requesting that one be sent to me] and have provided the clinical information described above as my explanation and supporting records. [If Dr. Okafor or his office is submitting or assisting with this appeal on my behalf, a signed Provider Permission Form is enclosed.]

Please send your acknowledgment of receipt and your decision to the address above, and please contact me at [member phone number] or [member email address] with any questions or if additional information is needed.

Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter.

Sincerely,

Avery Lawson
Member ID: W601208268

Enclosures: MRI report (2026-05-28); physical therapy discharge note (2026-03-10–2026-06-30); medication/injection records; exam notes; [surgeon letter of medical necessity]; copy of denial notice; [Medicaid Appeal Form]; [Provider Permission Form, if applicable]
